plainTranslation: The Moon person and Sun person often stand on opposite sides of the same room: one leading from feeling, one from identity. The attraction can be strong because each carries what the other notices. The work is trading perspective instead of casting one person as too needy or too self-focused.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.
note: Synced from authored synastry bundle synastry-authored__19_ (2).json.
summaryShort: Their moods, needs, and habits of comfort press against your sense of self, confidence, and direction.
summaryDeep: Their moods, needs, and habits of comfort press against your sense of self, confidence, and direction. It catches often enough that you both feel it, and it keeps asking to be worked out. Name it directly instead of letting it build in silence.
tension: The problem is that it can turn into a standoff. One person feels unseen. The other feels like nothing they do is enough.
advice: Don't make it a competition over whose needs matter more. Say what you need, listen to what they need, and meet somewhere in the middle.
